purpose: What wave 18 LEARNED while executing, kept apart from what it PREDICTED before executing. The frozen forecast is immutable; falsifications are recorded here so a reader at HEAD can tell the two apart without consulting git history.
rule_this_establishes: Frozen forecasts are immutable. Falsifications discovered during execution are recorded in a sibling execution-notes artifact, linked to the frozen forecast and the baseline commit.

baseline_observations.method: `classify_stack_tensor_on(relative_name, operator)` called directly against real safetensors headers. It has to be direct: `opplan::build` returns on the residual-topology refusal before reading any operand, so a hyper-connection checkpoint emits no UnclassifiedOperand for its HC tensors and that absence is structural silence, not evidence. Same move `k3_representable.rs` makes one stage down, for the same reason.
baseline_observations.fixture: scripts/hc_header_fixture_export.py fetches the shard headers over HTTP range requests; no payload is read. 130 tensors across three checkpoints, indexed families capped at two real members.

evidence: 0.self_attn.q_proj.weight -> AttnQ under Softmax and MlaQProj under Mla — operator awareness is live, not assumed

forecast_falsifications.prediction: 'no placement rule owns the hc_attn_*, hc_ffn_* and hc_head_* tensor groups' — one gap, one mechanism
forecast_falsifications.reason: Three stages, and the gap splits across two. `graph::build::classify_group` owns tensor-GROUP placement (failure: UnplacedGroup) and does block top-level hc_head_*. `plan` owns config semantics and physical SegmentTensor {name,dtype,shape,offset,len} — bytes, never meaning. `opplan::build` owns semantic role binding via the operator-aware classify_stack_tensor_on (failure: ClosureDefect::UnclassifiedOperand). The layer-level hc_attn_*/hc_ffn_* groups are ALREADY physically placed by the `layers` prefix; their unresolved plane is role classification, not placement.

forecast_falsifications.prediction: GLM-5.3-Flash's layer HC tensors should surface as UnclassifiedOperand today
forecast_falsifications.reason: opplan::build returns on the residual-topology refusal before any operand is read — its own comment says so. The general lesson, beside #415's: absence of a downstream defect does not imply downstream capability when an earlier refusal prevents the observation from being made.

forecast_falsifications.prediction: mtp.0 is a silent-omission trap; prove HC total-fate matching catches its 18 tensors
forecast_falsifications.reason: COMPONENT_EXTERNAL_NAMESPACES = ["mtp"] is checked BEFORE the group-pattern scan precisely because `mtp.layers` contains 'layers' and would otherwise merge a distinct sub-model into the primary DecoderStack. DeepSeek already reports `mtp` as one honestly-unplaced group (finding 72), and graph::tests::build already pins the whole family as unplaced. The correct invariant is the opposite: adding HC role recognition must NOT give any mtp.* tensor a primary-stack fate.

forecast_falsifications.prediction: DeepSeek-V4-Flash is wave 18's subject; it needs 'attn_norm/ffn_norm spellings' alongside HC placement
forecast_falsifications.result: false, and the understatement was large
forecast_falsifications.reason: DeepSeek's ENTIRE tensor dialect is foreign — attn.wq_a, attn.wq_b, attn.wkv, attn.wo_a, attn_norm, ffn.experts.N.w1. Measured overlap with the role vocabulary is exactly ONE operand on layer 0: ffn_norm.weight -> PostAttentionNorm. Adding HC roles would move DeepSeek from 'all unclassified' to 'nearly all unclassified', attributing nothing. The forecast centred DeepSeek because wave 17's arithmetic ORACLE came from DeepSeek's reference; that is the right source for arithmetic and the wrong specimen for addressability.

forecast_falsifications.result: nearly — two, and the second is pinned
forecast_falsifications.reason: GLM-5.3-Flash is FP8, so each mlp.*_proj carries a weight_scale_inv block-scale sidecar, and those three are unaddressed for reasons unrelated to residual topology. The baseline pins all NINE unclassified operands rather than the six, so a wave-18 rule loose enough to swallow a scale sidecar fails the assertion instead of passing a narrower one.

preserved_question: Unchanged from the frozen forecast: can a declared hyper-connection topology acquire complete executable carriage — semantic operand roles entering the normal closure — without collapsing the namespace, payload, or execution boundaries? Only the specimen changed, because the originally chosen one cannot isolate the variable.

implementation_findings.written: 2026-09-05, with the code, before the sweep was re-run
what_landed: Six OperandRoles — HcAttnMixFn, HcAttnBase, HcAttnScale, HcFfnMixFn, HcFfnBase, HcFfnScale — bound to the exact bare leaves `hc_{attn,ffn}_{fn,base,scale}` in ROLE_TABLE. Layer-blind (GLM's KDA and MLA layers each carry all six). The role carries no dtype: F32 on DeepSeek, BF16 on GLM, asserted from the headers.

ObjectKind::HyperConnectionHead — the head's three BARE groups (`hc_head_{fn,base,scale}`, DeepSeek's spelling) become one object with three bindings, placed ONLY when the artifact's resolved residual topology is HyperConnection. Without the declaration the groups stay unplaced and the reason names the disagreement. Hy4-preview's `model.hc_head` spelling is not in the table and its topology resolves to none, so it is untouched.

opplan::build no longer refuses on the topology. Closure runs: the six roles are required on every transformer layer of a hyper-connected component; the same six are `OperandImpliesAbsentOp` strays on a single-stream component; geometry is checked against the DECLARED stream count — mix_fn `[(2+hc)·hc, hc·hidden]`, base `[(2+hc)·hc]`, scale `[3]`; the head against `[hc, hc·hidden]`, `[hc]`, `[1]`. A hyper-connected component's mixer-only or conv-QKV layer is refused as unjudged.

The plan carries the bundle: `ComponentOpPlan.residual_topology`, `LayerPlan.hyper_connection { attention, ffn }` with three OperandRefs each, `ComponentOpPlan.hyper_connection_head`. Single-stream plans serialise byte-identically (the new keys are skipped).

The refusal moved, it did not disappear. `PreparedOperands::load` refuses a hyper-connected plan before loading one operand, reading `ResidualTopology::unimplemented_reason` — the same authority the plan report reads — whose text now names the TRAVERSAL as what is missing, neither the arithmetic (wave 17) nor the placement (wave 18). The production encode gate also still refuses the container as inadmissible (the three hc_* keys and the surface finding block).

the_instrument_was_mutation_tested_again.executor refusal disabled: CAUGHT — `an_addressable_topology_is_still_refused_at_the_executors_door` fails; the single-stream control in the same test still executes, so the failure is the refusal's absence and not a broken store.
the_instrument_was_mutation_tested_again.head placement ungated from the declarat: CAUGHT — `head_operands_without_the_declaration_stay_unplaced_with_the_disagreement_named` and `deepseeks_head_loses_its_owner_when_the_topology_is_not_declared` fail; the twelve other carriage tests pass, so the head can be placed for the wrong reason without any positive test noticing — the controls are what see it.
the_instrument_was_mutation_tested_again.the four closure refusals: each has its own test that fires it alone on the synthetic estate: a missing site operand (MissingOperand{HcFfnScale}), a Sinkhorn-free `[2·hc, hc·hidden]` mix projection (GeometryMismatch vs `[24, 256]`), a two-entry scale (GeometryMismatch vs `[3]`), a head stored at a site's geometry (two GeometryMismatches), site operands on a single-stream component (six OperandImpliesAbsentOp naming the topology).

implementation_findings.the_mtp_leak_test_the_baseline_could_not: Written now, on DeepSeek-V4-Flash's real headers: the head's three bare groups are owned, the layer sites sit in the decoder stack, `mtp` stays unplaced with its original reason, no object binding starts with `mtp`, and every hyper-connection tensor on the surface has exactly one fate (owned XOR external).

k3_transfer_measured.expected_by_the_k3_programme: the four `*_res_{norm,proj}` operands on K3's KDA layer are hyper-connection operands; wave 18's generic roles should address them, leaving `g_proj` alone (`plan::tests::k3_representable::KDA_LAYER_UNADDRESSED`).
k3_transfer_measured.measured: Zero of four moved, and `k3_kda_operands_are_addressed_except_the_five_named_deltas` still passes UNCHANGED. Read from K3's own headers: `self_attention_res_norm.weight` is `[7168]` and `self_attention_res_proj.weight` is `[1, 7168]` (same for `mlp_res_*`). A Sinkhorn site's mix projection is `[(2+hc)·hc, hc·hidden]`, which equals `[1, 7168]` for NO stream count (hc=1 gives `[3, 7168]`). They are a different residual topology — K3's config calls it AttnRes (`attn_res_block_size`, `output_attn_res_proj`, already in the ResidualWiring semantic cluster) — not this one's second dialect.
k3_transfer_measured.how_to_read_it: This is the 'fewer than 4 gone' arm of the K3 witness's own tripwire, and it is NOT accommodation: no K3-shaped name entered wave 18's vocabulary and the abstraction did not bend. The generic abstraction had nothing to transfer to, because the premise that K3's residual operands are Sinkhorn hyper-connections was a classification made at K3-ARCH-1 without reading their shapes — exactly the discoverable baseline fact the new doctrine says to measure rather than forecast. The four operands belong to a K3 rung of their own (a third residual topology, AttnRes), beside K3-REP-GATE-1 and K3-LATENTMOE-1, and its arithmetic is unread.
k3_transfer_measured.pinned_by: `opplan::tests::wave18_hc_carriage::k3s_residual_operands_are_not_sinkhorn_sites_under_any_stream_count` — both halves: no spelling classifies under Kda, and no stream count from 1 to 16 makes the shapes a site's.

implementation_findings.success_claim: LARQL can assign semantic operand identity to the Sinkhorn hyper-connection vocabulary and carry those operands through its normal execution-planning machinery, demonstrated on GLM and transferred independently to K3.
implementation_findings.success_claim_as_measured: The first clause holds on GLM-5.3-Flash's real headers (six operands to six named roles, three FP8 sidecars unmoved) and on DeepSeek-V4-Flash's (same six roles from a different path and dtype; head placed under the declaration; mtp external), and the carriage clause holds on a synthetic estate that declares the topology (closure holds, the plan carries the bundle, the executor refuses). The transfer clause does NOT hold as written: K3's residual operands are not instances of this vocabulary, so there was nothing to transfer to — see k3_transfer_measured.
implementation_findings.explicit_non_claim: Wave 18 does not make DeepSeek-V4 plannable. DeepSeek-V4 remains blocked by an independently unsupported base tensor dialect; its reference implementation supplied Wave 17's arithmetic oracle, not Wave 18's addressability witness.

three_kinds_of_evidence_from_three_model.DeepSeek: tells us what the Sinkhorn HC computation MEANS (wave 17's oracle), and now that its head and sites are addressable under its own dialect's spellings — while its base dialect keeps it blocked.
three_kinds_of_evidence_from_three_model.GLM: cleanly tells us whether HC semantic addressability works — the controlled subject, one variable moved.
three_kinds_of_evidence_from_three_model.K3: was to tell us whether the addressability transfers beyond the primary subject; it told us instead that its residual topology is a different one.

implementation_findings.future_closure_condition: A DeepSeek dialect rung that makes its base operands plannable should let the wave-18 HC roles attach with no new HC-specific work, so wave 17's arithmetic and wave 18's addressability meet on the original DeepSeek checkpoint. If that happens without touching roles.rs or graph::build's head rule, the decomposition was real.

doctrine_from_wave_19_onward.rule: Measure the baseline; forecast the intervention. Never forecast discoverable baseline mechanics.

doctrine_from_wave_19_onward.the_forecast_then_predicts_only_the_tran: Given baseline X, intervention Y should produce delta Z while controls A/B remain unchanged.
doctrine_from_wave_19_onward.why: Wave 18's five falsifications were all statements about the existing system, measurable before preregistration. The hypothesis survived; the model of the starting state failed. Wave 18 is the evidence for the rule.
